text:
alex: Heads-up — opened a docs PR to add a streaming example that demonstrates function calls + automatic fallback to a quantized variant when Dedicated capacity is saturated. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1234 :eyes:

maria: Nice. Can you include the SDK streaming snippet and a note about which model variants are compatible with fallback?

alex: Yep. Added an SDK snippet and a small compat table in the PR description. The snippet shows the client switching to `orion-xl-quant` if `orion-xl` returns a 429 or runtime fallback.

ben: Saw lint failures in the docs CI — docbot flagged the code fence language for the Python snippet. Also, the example used `stream=True` which our new SDK v2 uses `streaming=True`.

alex: Good catch, fixing now. Will push a follow-up commit to update the param and the fenced language.

docbot: CI: docs-lint failed on files/docs/model-catalog/streaming-fallback.md: code-fence-language (python3 -> python)

alex: Pushed fix for param and fences. Also added an explicit note about model-card fields: `fallback_model` (string) and `fallback_condition` (enum) so catalog consumers can opt in.

sorin: Quick question — does the fallback preserve KV cache or do we have to rewarm the quantized model? Important to call out for long-context apps.

lina: If we rewarm heavily, unit cost changes. Can we add a mini-benchmark line: 1) cold-start tokens/sec, 2) warmed KV tokens/sec for both float and quant variants? Otherwise customers will be surprised.

alex: Agree. I'll add a short table with two rows (cold/warmed) and reference the benchmark harness we used. Example numbers are placeholders until eng-ml confirms: float: cold 180 tok/s, warmed 1200 tok/s; quant: cold 300 tok/s, warmed 950 tok/s.

maria: For the migration guide: include a small checklist for Dedicated -> Private migrations (pin `fallback_model` to a local quant build, validate KMS keys, confirm image versions). A one-line sample command to run the compatibility check would help.

alex: Adding that. Proposed command in docs: `./dev-tools/model-check --model orion-xl --target quant --mode compatibility` and `./dev-tools/bench --model orion-xl --seq 4096 --warm 1`

ben: One more: link fix — the PR referenced the old runtime-compatibility doc at /docs/runtime/compat which now 301s. Point it to /docs/platform/runtime-compatibility. I left an inline comment in the PR.

alex: Fixed links and addressed all inline comments. Marked the PR ready for review.

maria: I'll review after lunch. If no blockers, we can merge and publish a small blog blurb about fallback behavior next week. :thumbsup:

sorin: Also add a short note about SLA impact (fallback to quant is best-effort and can change latencies). Keep the language explicit so platform teams can make an informed choice.

alex: Will add SLA note and a sample policy snippet for the console rollout rules.

maria: Thanks — adding to my review checklist.

docbot: PR update: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1234 — checks: docs-lint ✅, links ✅, ci-build ✅

alex: Merged after maria's review. Leaving an entry in the docs changelog and pinging product for the blog list. Thanks all! :party:
